messages.text: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map') in OrderList.jsx
That usually means the orders prop is undefined on the first render. How is it fetched?
useEffect with fetch, then setOrders
Initialise the state with an empty array: useState([]). Before the fetch resolves, orders is undefined otherwise.
it was useState() yeah. fixed
Good. You may also want a loading state so the list doesn't flash empty.
how would that look
Add const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true), set it to false after setOrders, and render a spinner while it's true.
done. now the spinner never goes away when the fetch fails
Move setLoading(false) into a finally block so it runs on success and on error.
and show an error message?
Keep an error state: catch the error, setError(err.message), and render it instead of the list when it is set.
done, thanks
You're welcome.

why: Pure debugging of a JavaScript error; nothing about the user.

messages.text: ssh to one of my boxes keeps timing out after the key rotation
Where do the servers run, and how are the keys distributed?
all my servers are on Hetzner, everything is managed with Ansible from the infra-live repo. the rotation playbook pushed the new keys yesterday
Then check whether the playbook replaced authorized_keys on that host. Run ssh -v and see which key it offers.
it offers the old key. my laptop is NixOS and I guess the agent still has the old one loaded
Likely. Remove the old identity with ssh-add -d and add the new one, or update the identity file in your NixOS ssh config so it survives a rebuild.
fixed, it was the nix config
Good. Worth adding the key path to the infra-live README so the next rotation doesn't trip on it.
can the playbook also remove the old key from the agent on my laptop?
Not cleanly, since the laptop isn't in the inventory. Better to make the playbook print a reminder, or manage the key path in your NixOS config only.
ok, the nix config is the source of truth for my machines anyway
Then point the identity file at a stable path and have the rotation playbook write the new key there.

why: User described their stable infrastructure: Hetzner servers, Ansible repo, NixOS at home.

messages.text: I need revenue per product category for last quarter, tables are orders, order_items, products

Something like: SELECT p.category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id WHERE o.created_at >= '2026-07-01' AND o.created_at < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY p.category;
need to exclude cancelled orders
Add AND o.status <> 'cancelled' to the WHERE clause.
and sort by revenue

messages.text: can you explain what a reverse proxy does
A reverse proxy sits in front of your servers and receives requests on their behalf, then forwards them to the right backend. It often handles TLS, caching and load balancing.
thanks. btw, reply in Dutch from now on unless it's code

top. wat is dan het verschil met een load balancer?
Een load balancer verdeelt verkeer over meerdere servers. Veel reverse proxies doen dat ook, maar een reverse proxy kan daarnaast TLS afhandelen, cachen en requests herschrijven.

messages.text: how do I make a subcommand optional with clap derive?
Wrap the subcommand field in Option: `command: Option<Commands>`. When it is None, run your default behaviour.
cool. context: this is for tidy-tabs, my rust CLI for cleaning CSVs. it's at about 400 stars now so I don't want to break the existing interface
Then keep the current flags on the top-level struct and add the subcommands alongside them, so existing invocations still parse.
will that conflict with positional args?
It can. If the top level takes a positional file path, set `args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true` so clap knows which form is meant.
makes sense, thanks
Add a test that runs the old invocation so a future change can't silently break it.

messages.text: my api container can't reach postgres in compose, connection refused on localhost:5432

Yes. api has no healthcheck, so it only reports running.

messages.text: my pandas groupby gives NaN for some students
Can you share the code and a few rows of the data?
df.groupby('student')['score'].mean() and some scores are the string 'absent'
Those strings make the column an object dtype. Convert with pd.to_numeric(df['score'], errors='coerce') before grouping.
that works. I teach high school chemistry and do this every term for grading, so I'll be back with more of these
Happy to help. If the sheet layout stays the same each term, a small script could do the whole grading pass in one go.
actually can we start now? columns are student, test, score, max_score
Sure. Compute a percentage per row with score / max_score, then average per student: df.assign(pct=df.score / df.max_score).groupby('student').pct.mean().
some tests count double though
Add a weight column and use a weighted mean: (pct * weight).sum() / weight.sum() per student, via groupby().apply().
works. and round to one decimal
Wrap it in round(..., 1), or call .round(1) on the resulting series.
